summary: Improvement remains strategically coherent and the codified priority order is still correct. TOP_PRIORITIES.md was refreshed against the full product stack and current TDE execution reality; no stale or incorrect priority ordering was found, so the canonical priority surface remains unchanged. Priority 1 is still the strongest structural bottleneck, but the Phase 1 canonical TDE-first substrate is now selected, validated, and aligned across plan, operating model, interfaces, decisions, and TDE entry surfaces. Priority 3 materially strengthened again on 2026-03-22: the rollout now explicitly covers Delivery, the completed package is published as the standard reference set, the Improvement-side interface language was tightened from future intent to active requirement, and the operating model now carries the maintenance rule. Priority 2 remains the clearest unchanged gap: pinned-lane delivery into PXS with version truth, rollback semantics, and verification still has no visible execution evidence.
materialChanges: TOP_PRIORITIES.md was reviewed against PRODUCT.md, MODEL.yaml, VISION.md, STRATEGY.md, OPERATING_MODEL.md, PLAN.md, RISKS.md, METRICS.md, INTERFACES.md, DECISIONS.md, Priority 3 execution artifacts, and current TDE runtime state; no stale or incorrect priority wording was detected, so the canonical priority surface remains unchanged.

Priority 3 advanced from partial rollout to completed active-product coverage: Delivery is now an explicit fifth product-side deployment step, which closes the remaining first-deployment gap across currently active products with canonical TOP_PRIORITIES surfaces.
The completed rollout package is now codified as the standard reusable reference set for future product-side deployment, review, and closure-evidence enforcement.

Improvement-side source-of-truth artifacts were tightened on 2026-03-22: INTERFACES.md now states the minimum interface as a current requirement, and OPERATING_MODEL.md now embeds the reuse-and-correct maintenance rule.
Priority 2 still shows no new distribution-path evidence; interim-copy drift exposure remains the main unchanged execution risk.

topPriorities.title: Converge improvement execution into one canonical TDE-first system of record
topPriorities.why: Improvement still needs one explicit, reusable, evidence-backed execution path; otherwise signals can fragment across non-canonical surfaces and weaken traceability.
topPriorities.currentStatus: The low-risk Phase 1 substrate is selected in D-003 and is now supported by PLAN, OPERATING_MODEL, INTERFACES, TDE entry-surface alignment, and exemplar validation around OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069. The main remaining gap is disciplined ongoing reuse and enforcement rather than substrate ambiguity.
topPriorities.nextStep: Use the now-aligned Phase 1 substrate and standard reference set as the bounded base for future product-side improvement routing, review, and closure-evidence enforcement.

topPriorities.title: Ship A-005 into PXS through a pinned lane with version truth, rollback, and verification semantics
topPriorities.why: Improvement delivery still depends on interim-copy behavior, so downstream drift risk remains active and installed-state truth is weak.
topPriorities.currentStatus: No new progress is visible in the reviewed product stack or execution evidence. Interim-copy lanes still appear to be the baseline mechanism, and the pinned-lane target is not yet the lived distribution path.
topPriorities.nextStep: Implement the pinned lane as an operational path with machine-checkable installed-version truth, explicit rollback behavior, and a verification pass that closes the interim-drift gap.

topPriorities.title: Roll out the minimum improvement interface across active products, starting with mandatory incident-to-improvement conversion
topPriorities.why: The proof case, intake contract, deployment coverage, and maintenance rule now exist, but portfolio value depends on sustained reuse and drift correction rather than one-off rollout notes.
topPriorities.currentStatus: IMP-ERR-20260315 remains the completed proof case. OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069 remain the validated reference intake batch. OPS-2026-070 has now produced rollout seed, five product-side deployment steps, a standard reference set, conformance tightening, and operating-model alignment. The bounded rollout now spans all currently active products with canonical TOP_PRIORITIES surfaces.
topPriorities.nextStep: Apply the operating-model maintenance rule opportunistically during future product reviews and product-surface edits, reusing the standard reference set and correcting any drift at the point of change.

constraints: Improvement must remain evidence-backed and must not become a narrative-only reporting layer.
Improvement does not own canonical task or decision state; that boundary remains with Task Management / TDE.
No authority or security boundary changes should be made as part of improvement rollout without explicit escalation.
